name: Surface O2 aeration (Henry's-law relaxation; mg/L units, temperature-bounded)

provenance.ref: Henry's law surface gas exchange dO2=kLa(O2sat-O2)
Dissolved-oxygen solubility in fresh water, 1 atm; standard tabulated mg/L vs degC

provenance.source: Stumm & Morgan, Aquatic Chemistry (3rd ed., 1996), redox-sequence ladder
provenance.ref: surface aeration equilibrates water with atmospheric O2, holding an OXIC redox poise in the oxidizing window Eh ~ +50..+500 mV; incompatible with strict-anaerobe habitats (methanogenesis, Eh < -200 mV)

notes: A dimensioned-units box: it speaks three non-canonical units at once (O2 in mg/L, temperature in degC, pressure in atm), exercising affine and molar-mass unit conversion at the medium boundary (mg/L to mmol via O2's molar mass, degC to K with the affine offset, atm to bar). O2 saturation uses real Benson-Krause/USGS solubility data (mg/L vs degC at 1 atm, in params.O2_solubility_mgL) scaled by pressure per Henry's law; kLa is a system-specific transfer coefficient. Declares temperature and pressure validity domains.

validity.note: Henry's-law saturation is temperature- and pressure-specific; O2_sat_ref=9.1 mg/L at 20 degC, 1 atm. Valid in liquid water 0-40 degC, ~0.5-2 atm.
